chunks: 'Ali b. Ahmad b. 'Abdullah b. Ahmad b. Abi 'Abdullah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from his grandfather Ahmad b. Abi 'Abdullah from Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Qurashi from Muhammad b. Sinan from 'Abdullah b. Talha and Isma'il b. Jabir and 'Ammar b. Marwan from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him):

'Isa b. Maryam (peace be upon him) went forth to fulfill a need of his, and he had three of his companions with him. He passed by three bars of gold on the road. So, 'Isa (peace be upon him) said to his companions: Surely, this kills people. Then, he continued walking. So, one of them said: I have a need. So, he left. Then, another one said: I have a need. So, he left. Then, the last one said: I have a need. So, he left. The three of them had gone to the gold. Two of them said to one: Buy us food. So, he went to buy food for them. He put poison in it so that he may kill them and not share the gold. The two said: When he comes, let us kill him so that we do not have to share. When he came, they went to him and killed him. Then, they ate, and they both died. So, 'Isa (peace be upon him) returned to them, and they were dead around it. So, he resurrected them by the permission of Allah the Exalted; then said: Did I not tell you that this kills people?!

key_terms.فَأَحْيَاهُمْ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: resurrected them by the permission of Allah -- one of 'Isa's miracles in Islamic tradition
key_terms.لَبِنَاتٍ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ: bars (bricks) of gold -- the physical temptation that drives the plot
key_terms.يَقْتُلُ النَّاسَ: kills people -- 'Isa's metaphorical warning that gold is deadly

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Prophet Isa and the three bars of gold in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: In this parable narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), Prophet 'Isa (Jesus, peace be upon him) and three companions encounter three bars of gold on the road. 'Isa warns that gold kills people, and walks on. But all three companions secretly return to the gold, each pretending to have other business. Driven by greed, each plots to eliminate the others: the one sent to buy food poisons it, while the other two plan to kill him on his return. The result is mutual destruction -- the buyer is murdered, and the two who eat the poisoned food die. When 'Isa returns and finds them all dead around the gold, he resurrects them by Allah's permission and reminds them of his warning. The story powerfully illustrates how the love of wealth (hubb al-dunya) leads to betrayal, murder, and self-destruction, vindicating 'Isa's prophetic insight.
